R176.rule: Never begin execution (spawning agents or swarms, running a migration, or making multi-file changes) without an explicit user go-ahead.

R177.rule: If you asked for a green light and the user's reply is anything other than a clear yes, keep planning and re-confirm before acting.

R178.rule: Always read a file before editing it.

R179.rule: Never commit secrets, credentials, or .env files.

R180.rule: Never save files to the root folder; use the designated directories instead.

R183.rule: Place documentation and markdown files in `/docs`.

R187.rule: Architect the project following Domain-Driven Design with bounded contexts.

R189.rule: Define typed interfaces for all public APIs.

R190.rule: Prefer TDD London School (mock-first) testing for new code.

R191.rule: Implement state changes using event sourcing.

R192.rule: Ensure input validation occurs at system boundaries.

R193.rule: Always run tests after making code changes.

R194.rule: Always verify the build succeeds before committing.

R195.rule: Never narrow the Verdaccio bind from `*:4873` to loopback only.

R196.rule: Never suggest starting or stopping the Verdaccio instance, which is always running.

R197.rule: If `localhost:4873` hangs while the LAN or Tailscale IP responds 200 on `/-/ping`, diagnose the shadowing second listener with `lsof -nP -iTCP:4873 -sTCP:LISTEN`.

R198.rule: When a VS Code Remote auto-forward is shadowing `127.0.0.1:4873`, fix it by stopping that forward in VS Code's Ports panel.

R199.rule: In feature work, create or update tests before implementing the change.

R200.rule: After implementing a feature change, run the tests and verify they pass.

R201.rule: After tests pass, run the build and verify it succeeds.

R202.rule: Never hardcode API keys, secrets, or credentials in source files.

R203.rule: Never commit .env files or any file containing secrets.

R204.rule: Always validate user input at system boundaries.

R205.rule: Always sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal.

R206.rule: Run `ruflo security scan` after making security-related changes.

R207.rule: Batch all independent operations into a single message.

R208.rule: Spawn all agents in one message using the Agent tool with `run_in_background: true`.

R209.rule: Batch all independent file reads, writes, and edits into one message.

R210.rule: Batch all independent Bash commands into one message.

R211.rule: For a single file edit or fix, work directly without spawning agents.

R212.rule: For work touching 3+ files, a new feature, or cross-module refactoring, spawn agents.

R213.rule: When in doubt about task complexity, start working directly and escalate to agents only if the scope grows.

R214.rule: Use `hive-mind_spawn` (or `ruflo hive-mind spawn --claude`) when convening a council with named experts, per-question voting, Byzantine consensus, and queen synthesis.

R215.rule: Do not call `swarm_init` reflexively at task start (applies to flat-coordination swarms only).

R216.rule: After spawning agents, stop and wait for the results.

R217.rule: Do not poll agent status after spawning agents.

R218.rule: When you need a capability, choose tools in the listed order and stop at the first match.

R219.rule: Assume sub-agents spawned via the `Agent` tool inherit the parent's `mcp__ruflo__*` toolset.

R220.rule: For long-running sub-tasks where MCP visibility is uncertain, run a discovery probe before spawning instead of pre-fetching results.

R221.rule: When the active toolset doesn't cover a needed capability, first run `ruflo skill list` to check whether a skill provides it.

R222.rule: If no skill covers the needed capability, run `ruflo plugins list` to check whether an installable plugin provides it.

R223.rule: Only after both the skill list and plugin list come up empty, build the missing capability inline or ask the user.

R224.rule: Never install a plugin without explicit user confirmation.

R225.rule: Install a plugin only when the user asked for a capability not covered by `ruflo skill list` or active MCP tools AND the user confirmed the install.

R226.rule: Never install from the upstream `@ruflo` marketplace; use the `sparkleideas` marketplace for plugins.

R227.rule: Never change plugin enable/disable state at user scope.

R228.rule: If plugin commands don't appear after installation, tell the user to run `/reload-plugins`.

R229.rule: Call ToolSearch to load a deferred `ruflo` MCP tool's schema before invoking it.

R230.rule: Do not call `mcp__ruflo__agentdb_session-start` or `mcp__ruflo__agentdb_session-end`; hooks manage session lifecycle automatically.

R231.rule: When a before-task `[INTELLIGENCE] Relevant patterns...` hook signal appears, incorporate it if relevant.

R232.rule: When a during-task `[INFO] Routing task...` hook signal recommends an agent type, consider using it.

R233.rule: Rely on hooks storing outcomes automatically after a task and do not call session-start/end yourself.

R234.rule: If `[INFO] Router not available` appears, proceed normally without routing.

R235.rule: Never run the one-time bootstrap `claude mcp add claude-flow -- npx -y @sparkleideas/ruflo@latest`; only the user runs it, once.
